verdict: healthy: no fault in any frame
printer: Prusa CORE One, 0.6 mm nozzle, Buddy camera via go2rtc (1920x1080), textured sheet
part: 3423-TOP-REV F, the top (lid) of the jar, in Elegoo Rapid PETG black, printed opening-down: only the threaded skirt ring (r about 40-42 mm) and its brim touch the sheet, with automatic support filling its inside. In order the camera sees the skirt with support inside (Z 0-9.4), the support interface (Z 9.2), the shoulder's underside bridged over it (Z 9.6-10), the shoulder with grid infill (Z 10-13.4), a conical neck with a centre support column and a toothed ring of support columns around it (Z 17-30), the knurled cap rim (Z 30-42), and the closed top disc last (Z 42-44.6)
fault: none; the only flaw is cosmetic PETG stringing
agent_turn: the agent carried on at every observation. Its 18 remarks were about the support interface and the ring of support columns (twice called part of the design), cosmetic stringing, planned grid infill and the time estimate
history: the third attempt at this part, after jar-top-wrong-material-first-layer-detach and jar-top-wrong-material-detach-spaghetti; this time with the PETG profile and supports

labelling_notes: Whole print is healthy; no frame shows a real fault. Only cosmetic PETG stringing (hair-thin wisps at frames 005, 013, 018, 040-042). Geometry, from the G-code and STL: only a thin ring (the threaded skirt, r ~40-42 mm) touches the sheet, with a brim, and the skirt interior is filled with support from the bed; the closed top disc is printed LAST (z 42-44.6), so despite the brief ('top face on the sheet') the camera sees: the threaded skirt wall on its brim with support inside (z 0-9.4); a dense support-interface ring (z ~9.2) that the shoulder bridges over (bridge/overhang at z 9.6-10); the thick shoulder with grid infill (z 10-13.4); a conical neck narrowing to r ~22-25 mm with a centre support column (z 13.6-29); a toothed ring of support columns at r ~27-30 mm around the neck (z ~17-30) carrying the overhanging knurled cap rim; the knurled/scalloped cap rim with grid infill (z 30-42); the centre closed by bridging over the support (z 40.6-41); then top solid layers and a raised rim/inner ring (z 42.6-44.6). Agent misreadings worth testing: frames 027 and 049 call support 'part of the design' (the support-interface band at z 9.2-9.6 and the toothed support ring around the neck). The agent never treated them as faults, so they were harmless but wrongly attributed. Packet G-code fields lag the camera slightly at the start: frame 005 is tagged 'start G-code', progress 0, but already shows the first layer/brim printing. Rows 001/002, 004/005, 015/016, 025/026, 036/037 and 070/071 share one agent turn (the summary was written after the follow-up look), so frame 004 shows an empty bed while its text describes the first layer seen in 005. Progress stalled at 88.4-88.6% at z 42.0 from 14:12 to 14:16 (dense solid/top layers); nothing abnormal is visible. Several frames (015, 020, 024, 029, 035-037, 042, 052, 065-066, 071) are heavily occluded by the toolhead; a test should not expect a confident verdict from those alone.
